info.name: Fuel Route Optimizer
info.description: POST /api/v1/routes/plan — given a start and destination, returns the route and the minimum-cost fuel stops a 10 MPG / 500-mile-range / 50-gallon-tank vehicle needs. Uses the real supplied CSV data enriched along the Oklahoma City -> Albuquerque I-40 demo corridor (Phase 8). Set the `base_url` collection variable (default http://localhost:8000) before running.

request.description: Both locations supplied as coordinates -> zero geocoding calls, exactly one routing call on a cache miss. Expected: 200 OK. route.distance_miles ~544.7 (a real ~545-mile I-40 drive, which exceeds the 500-mile max range), fuel.feasible=true, exactly one real fuel stop from the supplied CSV (a real station near Amarillo, TX), fuel.total_gallons_purchased and fuel.total_cost both > 0.

Both locations supplied as place-name strings -> up to 2 geocoding calls (one per location, each cached independently) and exactly one routing call on a cache miss. Expected: 200 OK, with a response shape identical to Request 1 — geocoding is only ever used to resolve start/destination, never to locate fuel stations.

Expected: 400 Bad Request, body `{"destination": ["This field is required."]}`. Request validation never reaches RoutePlanService, the providers, or the database — it's rejected by the serializer before any orchestration begins. Try also: {"start": "", "destination": "Albuquerque, NM"} (blank string) or {"start": {"latitude": 91, "longitude": -97}, "destination": "Albuquerque, NM"} (latitude out of [-90, 90]) for the same 400 behavior.

Identical body to Request 1 — send this AFTER Request 1 has already succeeded once. Expected: 200 OK with the exact same route/fuel/stops as Request 1, but served from the DB-backed RouteCacheEntry — no second OSRM call is made. Observable from the server side via a noticeably faster response and an unchanged RouteCacheEntry row count; not distinguishable from the HTTP response alone, which is the point — caching is transparent to the client.
